title: Penn State Wrestling's PJ Duke Explains His Match Mentality While Staying Consistent And Grounded - NewsBreak
text:
By Animesh Pandey ,
1 hours ago
Penn State wrestler PJ Duke recently opened up about his mentality for every wrestling match. The wrestler had recently been part of Penn State’s one-sided victory over Iowa.
Duke has been active on the wrestling circuit since 2010, when he was just 4 years old. The soon-to-be 20-year-old wrestler has been committed to the Nittany Lions since September 2023.
PJ Duke Opens Up On His Mentality Ahead Of Wrestling Duels In an Instagram reel shared by Penn State Wrestling, Duke opened up about dealing with every wrestling duel while staying grounded in approach. The teenage wrestler revealed in the reel about his approach as he stated,
“Yeah I kind of just treat every match the same. I try to at least, I’m sure Marcus is the same, uh we both have pretty similar mindsets so uh, no matter kind of where it is a practice or an actual match or whatever, just try to be the same person as always, and that kind of just helps you stay grounded and um, don’t let the fans get the match and stuff.”
READ MORE: What Cael Sanderson Said About Penn State Wrestling’s Growing Confidence After Iowa Win
Duke had previously been part of the Penn State squad when it faced the Northwestern Wildcats’ wrestling squad. The Nittany Lions continued their clean sweep streak as they pummeled the Wildcats by 51-0.
Duke’s Overall Track Record As A Wrestler Duke has been active in senior wrestling since 2024. The teenage wrestler attempted to qualify for the World Championships but wasn’t successful, finishing third in the trials.
Duke made up for the same with his performance at the U20 Pan American Championships held in Lima the same year, where he clinched the gold medal for the USA in men’s 70kg. freestyle.
The teenage wrestler underwent a remarkable transformation in 2025. He not only won the World Team trials, but also qualified for three formats of the World Championships, viz. The U20, the U23, and the senior version as well.
Duke won the U20 World Championship without any major trouble. He lost out on another consecutive gold medal in the U23 version, but made up for it with a bronze medal. Unfortunately, the 19-year-old wrestler didn’t taste success in the senior version. After winning the first round, Duke lost to Kazakh wrestler Nurkozha Kaipanov in the pre-quarterfinals of the 2025 World Wrestling Championships.
